title: Oh My Gut!: Things You Wish You Knew About Your Gut, Nutrition, and Mental Health.
description: Your everyday guide to the most important and overlooked organ in your body: a clear-eyed journey through the gut, including specially made recipes for Crohn’s, colitis, and IBS. In Oh My Gut! , health and digestion researcher Mili Levran explores the digestive system through an integrative lens of nutrition and the latest tools and tips on the mind-gut connection. Drawing on years of professional experience—as well as her family's personal journey through ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease—Mili answers some of the most important questions that we don’t ask about our most important organ: What role do gut bacteria play in overall health? How does chronic stress affect digestion and inflammation? Why do emotional experiences sometimes manifest as physical symptoms? And what can we do to support the body's natural ability to restore balance? Alongside nineteen of Mili’s own tasty, nutritious, healthy recipes designed to put as little stress on your gut as possible, Oh My Gut! will teach you about: The science of the gut-brain connection and the body's "second brain" The essential role of the microbiome in digestion, immunity, and overall wellness How to use methods from Chinese medicine to balance digestion and whole-body health Practical tools for supporting resilience, reducing inflammation, and improving daily well-being Strategies for developing a healthier relationship with your body and its signals Your gut influences more than just your digestion—it plays a vital role in your immune system, energy levels, mood, mental resilience, and far more. If you've ever felt stuck, overwhelmed, or frustrated with where you are, the problem isn't you. The problem is the power you give to other people. Two simple words— Let Them —will set you free. title: The Body Keeps the Score: Brain, Mind, and Body in the Healing of Trauma
description: #1 New York Times bestseller “Essential reading for anyone interested in understanding and treating traumatic stress and the scope of its impact on society.” —Alexander McFarlane, Director of the Centre for Traumatic Stress Studies A pioneering researcher transforms our understanding of trauma and offers a bold new paradigm for healing in this New York Times bestseller Trauma is a fact of life. Veterans and their families deal with the painful aftermath of combat; one in five Americans has been molested; one in four grew up with alcoholics; one in three couples have engaged in physical violence. Dr. Bessel van der Kolk, one of the world’s foremost experts on trauma, has spent over three decades working with survivors. In The Body Keeps the Score , he uses recent scientific advances to show how trauma literally reshapes both body and brain, compromising sufferers’ capacities for pleasure, engagement, self-control, and trust. He explores innovative treatments—from neurofeedback and meditation to sports, drama, and yoga—that offer new paths to recovery by activating the brain’s natural neuroplasticity. description: Your Anxious Brain Is Not Broken! Is anxiety robbing you of your life? Wearing you out? Always making you feel exhausted even when you're doing nothing? Is your body tensing up without you even noticing? Do you sometimes feel like all you want to do is lie in your bed? All curled up in a ball for the rest of your life? Anxiety is the silent monster of our times. Maybe you suffer from social anxiety, thinking everyone judges you, always, no matter who they are, even your closest friends. Or maybe you overthink situations so much it makes you anxious and you can't find relief… Sometimes you don't even want to get out of bed. But as you're lying there, your heart starts beating really fast and it becomes hard to breathe for no reason... It feels like sleep is the only thing that can bring you peace. You sleep for long hours just to escape the dreadful feeling… yet when you wake up, you're feeling even more tired than before. You just want your life back! And you're not alone! Over 275 million people around the world suffer from anxiety disorders. It might seem like a cruel joke, but anxiety was originally our body's alarm system, meant to keep us safe from the dangers of a harsh world. But in our modern, overstimulated world, this alarm doesn't know when to turn off. So if you want to bring your anxiety under control, you need to understand why your nervous system is stuck in fight-or-flight mode. It's why your brain tends to catastrophize and ruminate constantly. But here's the good news: your brain isn't static! It evolves. And through the power of Neuroplasticity, you have the ability to reshape it and create new, anxiety-free neural pathways. This is not just an empty promise; it's a scientific fact! title: Mental Health for Men: What Nobody Told You About Strength, Silence, and Why Carrying It A
description: You know something is not right. You are not falling apart visibly. You are showing up, handling it, keeping it moving, being useful, being fine. But underneath the fine, something is grinding. Mental Health for Men is a direct, practical book for men who were taught to push through, stay quiet, keep control, and call that strength. It does not ask readers to perform vulnerability or dress up pain in therapy language. It explains what is happening, why the old strategies stop working, and what a man can actually do next. Inside, readers explore: Why anger is often the only emotion men feel allowed to express, and what may sit underneath it. How depression, anxiety, stress, and shutdown can look different in men. The real cost of silence, performance, work addiction, isolation, and carrying everything alone. How upbringing, shame, pressure, and old survival rules shape adult reactions. What support, therapy, friendship, grief, and repair can look like without turning into a performance. How to build a life that holds, not just a routine that looks impressive. title: 500 Journal Prompts: For Mental Health, Creativity, and Personal Exploration
description: Do you want to journal but never know what to write about? Are you a therapist or coach and need topics to discuss with your clients? Do you need thought provoking questions to ask your podcast guests? I’ve got you covered! You’ve probably heard about the awesome benefits of journaling. As a psychologist, it is something that I suggest to just about every client that I work with. However, journaling can be quite a daunting task. If you are one of the many people that are terrified by the blank page and never know what to write about, I’ve got you covered! This is a collection of 500 prompts for you to reflect on. They are randomized so that you can flip to any page and find something to write about. The prompts include deep questions about your life, creativity exercises, and thought-provoking quotes. Whether you are a person looking to better understand yourself or a professional such as a therapist or coach, you will get a ton of value out of these prompts. Aside from journaling, these are also fantastic topics for podcast interviews or even conversation starters on a date. Sample Prompts: What is the most beautiful thing you have ever seen? Write a letter to yourself 5 years ago. Take a task that you’ve been dreading and break it up into the smallest possible steps. What do you need to give yourself more credit for? What are you waiting for? description: THE ACCLAIMED #1 NEW YORK TIMES BESTSELLER with over two million copies sold • A must-read for all parents: the generation-defining investigation into the collapse of youth mental health in the era of smartphones, social media, and big tech—and a plan for a healthier, freer childhood. • A cultural catalyst for the resulting $17.1 Billion Meta Settlement. Named one of the best books of the year by The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times Book Review, The Washington Post, Time, The Economist, New York Post , and Town & Country • One of Barack Obama’s Favorite Books of the Year • Named finalist for the PEN Literary Awards “With tenacity and candor, Haidt lays out the consequences that have come with allowing kids to drift further into the virtual world . . . While also offering suggestions and solutions that could help protect a new generation of kids.” — Time After more than a decade of stability or improvement, the mental health of adolescents plunged in the early 2010s. Rates of depression, anxiety, self-harm, and suicide rose sharply, more than doubling on many measures. Why? In The Anxious Generation , social psychologist Jonathan Haidt (pronounced "height") lays out the facts about the epidemic of teen mental illness that hit many countries at the same time. He then investigates the nature of childhood, including why children need play and independent exploration to mature into competent, thriving adults. Haidt shows how the “play-based childhood” began to decline in the 1980s, and how it was finally wiped out by the arrival of the “phone-based childhood” in the early 2010s. title: Stop Letting Everything Affect You: How to break free from overthinking, emotional chaos,
description: STOP LETTING EVERYTHING AFFECT YOU is a transformative guide for anyone who overthinks too often, gets stuck in emotional chaos, and finds themselves trapped in cycles of self-sabotage. With raw honesty and practical wisdom, Daniel Chidiac reveals why small things ruin your entire day and offers proven strategies to finally break free. This book will teach you how to: Stop letting little things ruin your entire day. Stop self-sabotaging. Set healthy boundaries without feeling guilty. Recognize the difference between real guilt and manipulation. Break the cycle of overthinking before it spirals out of control. Stop taking everything so personally and free yourself from emotional reactivity. Identify toxic patterns in relationships and walk away without regret. Be more in control and feel better everyday. Shift your mindset from victimhood to self-empowerment. Learn the art of emotional detachment—how to be unbothered without becoming cold. Move forward unapologetically, without feeling the need to explain your growth. Whether you're exhausted from overthinking everything, tired of absorbing everyone else's energy, or simply ready to stop letting life's chaos dictate how you feel, this book offers the transformative tools to finally reclaim your power, protect your peace, and live on your own terms. Your journey to inner strength and freedom starts here. Daniel Chidiac , International best-selling author of Who Says You Can't? You Do and The Modern Break-Up brings his new book, Stop Letting Everything Affect You . Do you wish you had clear, practical steps to manage depression, bipolar symptoms, or emotional spirals—without endless jargon or generic advice?
